# v0.9

Cost-aware GitOps Platform — portfolio/lab release, 2026-11-15.
Repository: https://github.com/workwithcrow12-art/cost-aware-gitops-platform
Python package version: `0.9.0`; release/image tag: `v0.9`.

## Changes

- Removed full card-number/CVV logging from the mock payment handler.
- Fixed session/currency cookie paths and logout for product deep links and prefixed deployments.
- Removed concurrent writes to frontend platform metadata and published immutable deployment snapshots atomically.
- Corrected zero multiplication and invalid fractional-money sign checks in both Go money packages; currency conversion preserves request cancellation.
- Rejected nonfinite OpenCost/CUR costs and malformed OpenCost allocation containers; zero and negative credits remain valid.
- Added regression tests for the fixes and a HIGH/CRITICAL Trivy gate for FinOps release images.
- Replaced the FinOps Debian slim base after its OS vulnerability scan failed, using the digest-pinned Python Alpine base already used by the application services. CI runs the full FinOps suite inside that runtime as well as the Python 3.12 compatibility check.
- Adapted workflows and Argo CD repository paths to the owner-selected monorepo. Nested component workflows are standalone examples, not active automation.

## Validation and publication contract

The local offline WSL pass completed 42 FinOps tests, 1 mocked bootstrap test and 10 release/smoke fixture tests. The bootstrap and FinOps suites passed again after their subsequent changes. Isolation used private network/PID/mount namespaces, read-only source/toolchain, an empty allowlisted environment, UID/GID 65534 with no capabilities, 128 MiB scratch, 512 MiB address space, 45 seconds CPU, 60 seconds wall-clock, 64 processes, 128 descriptors and 16 MiB maximum file size. Sandbox cleanup completed successfully.

The owner authorized ordinary GitHub-hosted CI with dependency/toolchain/CVE downloads. The active `Release validation` workflow checks:

- FinOps lint, unit tests, Custodian policy validation, fixture commands, container smoke checks and image scan;
- Go service tests with the race detector, Node tests, Python service tests, .NET cart tests and release/smoke fixtures;
- Terraform formatting, initialization without backend, validation, mock tests, TFLint, bootstrap tests and cost-tag policy tests;
- rendered Kubernetes/Helm manifests, Kyverno rules, pod restrictions and deployed Redis digest scans;
- builds and HIGH/CRITICAL scans of all 11 Boutique service images.

See [Actions](https://github.com/workwithcrow12-art/cost-aware-gitops-platform/actions) for current evidence. Source pushes are validation candidates. The tag workflow requires a successful `Release validation` push run for the current main SHA before publishing. It rebuilds and scans the images before pushing to GHCR, then creates the GitHub release only after every publication job succeeds. A tag alone does not prove the publication jobs completed.

## Using the release

Clone this repository and run component commands from their respective directories. Active CI is in `.github/workflows`. Argo CD paths include `gitops-config/`.

The release publishes `ghcr.io/workwithcrow12-art/<service>:v0.9` for each Boutique service and `ghcr.io/workwithcrow12-art/finops-toolkit:v0.9`. Scanned Boutique digest records are retained as release-workflow artifacts for reviewed GitOps promotion. The GitOps base remains pinned to upstream images until a deployment change is reviewed; publishing source/images does not modify a running cluster. GHCR package visibility and private registry pull credentials must match the intended deployment.

## Scope and remaining operator work

This is a focused source review and release validation, not a full security audit or production certification. No AWS/GKE/AKS infrastructure was provisioned. Actual cluster bootstrap, secrets, notifications, checkout smoke, rollback, persistence and recovery need separate deployment verification.

The supplied project review was substantially stale: Athena provisioning, Terraform lint/mock checks, Kyverno gates, restricted pods, Grafana dashboard, production Prometheus persistence, variable waste rates, currency normalization and failure notifications already existed. No duplicate modules, automatic credential rotation or obsolete PodSecurityPolicy were added.

Existing logs containing previously entered real payment data require a separate retention/access review; source fixes do not erase historical logs. Old deep-link cookies may need clearing after upgrade. The optional shopping assistant is not deployed by the base manifests; response-body cleanup remains to be addressed before enabling it. Image scans apply to the databases and versions used by that run and do not guarantee the absence of future vulnerabilities.
